incidents.vector: Intruders accessed the benefits-administration platform's network and exfiltrated files over a five-day window in November before the company was later listed on a ransomware leak site.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers, financial account details, health insurance and medical data, passport numbers and taxpayer IDs for tens of thousands of people were stolen; over 64,000 South Carolina residents were affected and class-action suits are forming.

incidents.vector: West Africa-linked syndicates ran business email compromise, romance and investment scams, laundering proceeds through electronic wallets, shell companies and money mules across dozens of countries.
incidents.impact: Interpol's Operation Jackal IV produced 58 arrests and identified 263 suspects; police seized millions in cash and crypto and blocked hundreds of bank accounts, with investigators noting the group's growing focus on sextortion of minors.

incidents.victim: UK power plant and US water utilities
incidents.vector: A MOIS-directed group compromised critical-infrastructure operators since 2023, reportedly abusing insecure operational technology such as programmable logic controllers running turbine and boiler systems.
incidents.impact: A small UK power plant was forced offline for four days (no grid outage), and Iranian actors have hit water systems in at least 12 US states; the US Treasury sanctioned six MOIS-linked operators on Aug 24 as part of a broad pressure campaign.

incidents.vector: A large distributed denial-of-service attack flooded the infrastructure of Digdir's IT partner Vivicta, two to three times larger than prior incidents.
incidents.impact: Ten digital services were disrupted for more than 30 hours, including the ID-porten identity gateway used by 4.5 million people, degrading access to public records, online pharmacies and the e-prescription system; no sensitive data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Overseas scammers impersonated law enforcement and government officials by phone and email, convincing victims to hand over cash and gold to a money mule who forwarded the funds to India.
incidents.impact: At least nine mostly elderly victims in New York and New Jersey lost more than $7.5 million; the accused mule, Jay Sunilbharthi Goswami, was arrested in Canada after fleeing the US and faces up to 20 years.

incidents.vector: Attackers used a social engineering attack in early July to breach the firm's cloud systems, part of a broader campaign targeting US investment and Wall Street firms.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen; Apollo confirmed the breach in a notice to the California attorney general, and the incident is one of several hitting the financial sector in the same wave.

incidents.vector: The attacker abused the protocol's own anti-theft defenses to trick the platform into issuing unwanted loans, reportedly using an AI tool to chain together six smaller unrelated bugs.
incidents.impact: Roughly $1.7 million in crypto-assets was stolen from the protocol.

incidents.victim: Drivers using DoFun Android car head units
incidents.vector: Attackers abused the legitimate TWCore update application on Chinese-made DoFun head units to silently push a malicious downloader (JarService) without any driver interaction.
incidents.impact: Infected in-car systems were conscripted into a proxy botnet linked to the BadBox operation, routing others' internet traffic through vehicles and generating fraudulent ad clicks; the vendor says it has fixed the issue.

incidents.victim: Global web servers (government, education, media, tech, gaming)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking group tracked as UAT-10147 exploited publicly disclosed vulnerabilities to gain remote code execution on Windows and Linux web servers, using AI-assisted tooling for exploitation, privilege escalation and payload generation.
incidents.impact: Attackers deployed BadIIS SEO-fraud malware and the new cross-platform SPECTRE backdoor (with credential theft and EDR-killer capabilities) for data theft and search-engine fraud, from a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs across Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam.

incidents.victim: Academia, aerospace/defense, government and think tanks (Europe and US)
incidents.vector: Three suspected Russian clusters (including one tied to the group formerly called APT29) ran persistent phishing campaigns that abuse legitimate authentication flows — app-password, OAuth and device-code phishing, plus WhatsApp device-linking — to hijack personal accounts and bypass two-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Individuals of interest to the Russian state had personal accounts compromised, with some operations also delivering malware and recording victims' audio and video after account takeover.

incidents.victim: The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), Toronto
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party software application used by the hospital.
incidents.impact: Personal data of hospital employees was stolen; the hospital says no patient data was exposed and is offering affected staff 24 months of credit and identity monitoring.

incidents.victim: US and foreign universities, companies and government agencies
incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran a years-long spearphishing campaign against professor accounts, largely on behalf of the IRGC, to harvest credentials and exfiltrate research and intellectual property.
incidents.impact: A superseding US indictment charged 17 members with stealing more than 31.5 terabytes of academic data and IP from 144 US and 178 foreign universities plus dozens of companies and agencies; the State Department offered up to $10 million for information on five defendants.

incidents.vector: North Korean IT-worker operators (tracked as PurpleDelta), likely based in China, used at least 22 fabricated personas with AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and forged IDs to win remote developer jobs and pass interviews.
incidents.impact: Operators were likely employed at ten or more organizations, recording internal meetings and using personal devices and bank accounts to funnel wages to the regime; separately, the FBI is investigating a North Korean IT staffer who worked for an unnamed US agency.

incidents.vector: Attackers registered their own Microsoft 365 tenant and posed as the victim's IT Service Desk, hosting a fake PowerShell 'maintenance tool' on legitimate Azure storage to deliver the modular SynkLoader implant.
incidents.impact: The multi-tool profiles the victim's network size, establishes stealthy persistence, and includes a convincing fake Windows lock screen ('PhishLocker') to harvest SSO passwords; researchers assess it likely sets the stage for follow-on ransomware.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack on the shipping giant disrupted operations and exposed customer data held for order fulfilment.
incidents.impact: At least eight European warehouses were affected and downstream companies reported theft of their customers' names, home addresses, phone numbers and email addresses, rippling across banks, retailers and gaming platforms.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack struck the ministry days before the country's presidential transition, one day after Colombia's national CERT warned of increased ransomware focus on the country.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted some services around illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the French telecom's systems and exfiltrated customer records.
incidents.impact: More than 2.1 million customers were affected, with stolen data including names, postal addresses, phone numbers, contract and connection details, and for some customers IP addresses and equipment details.

incidents.vector: North Korean espionage actors breached the Presidential Office in February as part of a broader campaign; authorities have not disclosed how initial access was gained.
incidents.impact: The intrusion was one of more than 100 victims by April, including universities, police departments, news agencies and hospitals; South Korean authorities are still investigating.
